The Top Must-Have Online Digital Marketing Tools & Resources to Put your Online Marketing Campaigns into Overdrive

I had a look at the list covered in the article and was like, "meh"!

So here's a list of my own:

Landing Pages

Unbounce

Make landing pages with minimum hassle and pull leads into whatever CRM you use. Also does A/B testing.

Lead Pages

Like Unbounce but cheaper.

CRM

Agile CRM

A full 360 degree sales and marketing app that integrates with your site to track user behaviour, capture leads, automate email marketing, deliver custom content and track sales through your marketing pipeline. Like Hubspot, but better.

Infusionsoft

Similar to Agile CRM

Email Marketing

Mailchimp

Winner, winner, chicken dinner! I've tried so many other email marketing platforms I've lost count. I keep coming back to Mailchimp because it's simply the best out there and plugs into everything.

Project Management

Asana

Need to keep tabs on your campaigns, manage external agencies and know what your team is doing at a glance? Asana is the tool. Replaces horrible email chains and allows you to set accountability and deadlines for key marketing tasks. Also plugs into Dropbox and Google Drive, which is nice!

Content

Feedly

If you're looking for content ideas Feedly is pretty good at recommending news and information sources in a number of verticals. Set it up, subscribe to feeds or add your own and check it when you need some inspiration.

PR

HARO

Yet to really use this but have anecdotal evidence that it works. Try it, you might like it.

SEO

Raven Tools

They do a decent job of uncovering technical issues with your site and helping you manage and track your link building campaigns. Good for teams but not so great if you're a one man marketing band.

AHREFS

SEO research can be a pain in the ass, especially when you're looking at competitor link profiles. MOZ and Raven both have reasonable indexes but IMO, AHrefs is the winner when it comes to backlink profile analisys and rank tracking.

Analytics

3 flavours, 2 paid, all slightly different.

Google Analytics

Vanilla, standard, does what is says on the tin but isn't hugely user friendly. It's free though, so there is that.

Mixpanel

If you market apps, this is for you. Gives you detailed info on things like installs, user behaviour, retention, etc etc and is infinitely tweak-able.

Kissmetrics

Used this with a couple of eCommerce sites to track customer behaviour and average transaction value against different paid and non paid traffic referrers, like Mixpanel it's a paid for service.

Social

Buffer

While I wouldn't recommend this for ALL your social activity, Buffer is a good way to schedule campaigns across Twitter and FB. If you want text book example of how to market a product and gain a bunch of users on almost zero budget, go check out their company blog. They're very good at what they do.

...I would add a bunch more, but I think that's enough already.
